quote: I just talked with Jake from ION.
stewart_read: Customer discloses a duplicate/prior touch; rep should probe what Jake covered and at what stage, not just confirm it happened.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be strategically deferring to check the system for a duplicate record before wasting the customer's time re-asking questions already answered.
coaching_implication: Ask directly: 'What did Jake go over with you already?' before disappearing to check the system.

quote: And Jake shots you a call?
stewart_read: Second touch on the same prior-contact signal; still only confirms the fact, no depth.
coaching_implication: This was the moment to ask if a bill or design had already been started with Jake — critical for not duplicating or dropping effort.

quote: Matter of fact, I was getting ready to send him a copy of my bill.
stewart_read: This is a live anchor — the customer is mid-bill-collection with another rep — and it is met with total silence for nearly 30 seconds.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have been occupied resolving the duplicate-record issue in the CRM at that exact moment, a system/technical gap rather than a conversational choice.
coaching_implication: Even mid-lookup, acknowledge verbally: 'Great, that'll help — let's make sure that gets to the right place.'

quote: just keep working with Jake. He he's got you set up, so I'll go ahead and get this clear.
stewart_read: Call ends with no next step owned by Gabe, no confirmation of what happens next for the customer, and no handshake.
coaching_implication: Even when redirecting to another rep, confirm the customer knows what to expect next (e.g., 'Jake will follow up with you on the bill you send him').

quote: I'll be super quick. I just have a couple questions.
stewart_read: Rep references the online form for legitimacy but frames the call as a quick transactional ask rather than establishing full context, which may have contributed to the customer's later confusion about duplicate contact.
alternative_hypothesis: The form-reference alone may be sufficient legitimacy per intros.standard; the confusion stemmed from the duplicate lead, not the intro itself.
coaching_implication: No major fix needed here — the duplicate-lead confusion is the bigger issue, but tightening the intro to mention timing/context could help avoid overlap confusion.
